title: Nobody told the ice maker to stop
description:
Four pounds a day: that's roughly what a refrigerator ice maker makes, according to GE Appliances. Leave it alone for a year and the math says about 1,400 pounds.

In real life, the ice maker stops when the bin is full (a little arm or sensor tells it). In this kitchen, nobody told it. He survived. The peas did even better.

Useless Facts: true numbers, used irresponsibly.

Sources:
- GE Appliances: Refrigerator - Normal Ice Production and Cube Size (about 4 pounds of ice per day): https://products.geappliances.com/appliance/gea-support-search-content?contentId=16918
- Whirlpool Product Help: Ice Cube Test, how much ice should my ice maker make (100-140 cubes in 24 hours): https://producthelp.whirlpool.com/Refrigeration/Full-Size_Refrigerators/Quad_Door_Refrigerator/Ice_and_Water_Concerns/Ice_and_Dispenser_Concerns/Ice_Production/Low_Ice_Production/Bottom_Freezer/Ice_Cube_Test_-_How_much_ice_should_my_ice_maker_make%3F
- Sub-Zero: Ice production and ice bucket capacity (in-unit ice makers stop producing once the bucket is full): https://www.subzero-wolf.com/assistance/answers/ice-production-and-ice-bucket-capacity

questions.q: How much ice does a refrigerator ice maker make per day?
questions.a: A typical home refrigerator ice maker makes about 3 to 4.5 pounds of ice a day; GE Appliances puts a standard crescent-cube ice maker at about 4 pounds.

questions.q: Does an ice maker stop when the bin is full?
questions.a: Yes. Refrigerator ice makers use a sensor or a feeler arm and stop making ice once the bucket is full, so the 1,400 pounds in the video is a joke, not a risk.

questions.q: How long does it take an ice maker to fill the bin?
questions.a: Whirlpool says it can take up to 2 to 3 days, depending on use, for a refrigerator ice maker to completely fill its bin.
